task_instance: GENERATE mode: generate a CI pipeline for a small Node.js library repository that has none. Created a realistic sample repo (string-utility library with package.json npm scripts for lint/test/build, source, a unit test, and plain-Node lint/build scripts), detected the forge, chose reasonable PR-and-push CI policy (no user available to answer the interactive questions), and produced a hardened GitHub Actions workflow validated with the real actionlint linter.
tools_used: actionlint (WASM build installed locally via npm)
evidence: Work dir real2_work/r245. Read SKILL.md and references/generate.md (all three reference files present). Built sample-repo/: package.json (scripts lint='node scripts/lint.mjs', test='node --test', build='node scripts/build.mjs'), src/index.js, test/index.test.js, scripts/lint.mjs, scripts/build.mjs, git-initialized with a GitHub-hosted origin remote. Verified the project automation really runs: 'npm run lint' -> 'lint ok'; 'npm test' -> 2 pass / 0 fail; 'npm run build' -> 'build ok -> dist/index.js'. Forge detected via the credential-safe host-only sed command from SKILL.md -> GitHub (code-hosting SaaS host), so GitHub Actions. Generated sample-repo/.github/workflows/ci.yml (52 lines) applying the skill principles: steps call the npm scripts rather than inline command logic; top-level 'permissions: contents: read' (least privilege); third-party actions (checkout, setup-node) pinned to full commit SHAs with a version comment; 'concurrency' group with cancel-in-progress; fail-fast DAG lint -> test -> build via 'needs'; no path filters because the repo is single-component; no secrets/registry/deploy because it is a library. VALIDATED the deliverable: installed the official actionlint as a locally-installed WASM npm package (actionlint 2.0.6, main.wasm 2.1MB) into the work dir's node_modules and ran it through a small Node runner (run-actionlint.mjs). Result: 'actionlint: no issues' (exit 0) on the generated workflow. Negative control: a deliberately broken workflow (job 'needs' a nonexistent job) was correctly flagged by the same actionlint, confirming it is the real linter and not a no-op. Step 5 cross-checks: every referenced automation target exists and runs; permissions minimal; no secrets required. Note: the action SHA pins use known release SHAs from prior knowledge; they could not be re-verified against the action registry offline because network/web lookups are disallowed by this run's rules, but this does not affect workflow validity. The interactive policy questions of GENERATE mode could not be answered by a user (none in session), so representative default policy choices were made; the core deliverable (a valid, hardened CI workflow) exists and was verified.
